User is interested in the Northern Ireland conflict (the Troubles) and the peace process, especially how political leadership shaped the British government's approach. #NorthernIreland #peaceprocess

User is interested in broader conflict resolution and peacebuilding, including whether Northern Ireland's peace factors (civil society, economic development, international engagement) transfer to other conflict zones. #conflictresolution #peacebuilding

Margaret Thatcher, UK PM 1979-1990, took a hardline approach in Northern Ireland: refused to negotiate with the IRA/Sinn Fein, backed a military campaign, and introduced the Prevention of Terrorism Act (1974). #NorthernIreland #Thatcher

Gerry Adams, Sinn Fein president 1983-2018, was key to the peace process: helped persuade the IRA to call a ceasefire in 1994 and helped negotiate the Good Friday Agreement in 1998. He was controversial over alleged IRA leadership. #NorthernIreland #GerryAdams
Tony Blair, UK PM 1997-2007, worked closely with Irish Taoiseach Bertie Ahern and was instrumental in securing the 1998 Good Friday Agreement. #NorthernIreland #TonyBlair #GoodFridayAgreement

Ian Paisley, founder and leader of the DUP, long opposed the peace process and refused to negotiate with Sinn Fein, but after the DUP became the largest Assembly party in 2007 he agreed to share power with Sinn Fein. #NorthernIreland #IanPaisley #DUP

David Cameron, UK PM 2010-2016, maintained commitment to the Northern Ireland peace process, but austerity cuts and especially the Brexit referendum raised concerns about destabilising the settlement and reintroducing a hard border with the Republic of Ireland. #NorthernIreland #DavidCameron #Brexit

Non-political factors credited with aiding the Northern Ireland peace process: civil society and reconciliation groups, international engagement (EU, US, UN), economic development and investment, and the security forces (controversial over human rights allegations). #NorthernIreland #peaceprocess

Challenges to applying Northern Ireland-style peacebuilding elsewhere: entrenched political/social polarisation, resource constraints and poverty, self-interested international interference, and deep cultural/historical hatred and mistrust. #peacebuilding #conflictresolution
User believes international interference by powerful states pursuing their own agendas is a major obstacle to peacebuilding, and asked how to mitigate it. #peacebuilding #conflictresolution

São Paulo's air quality measures include promoting public transportation, bike-sharing programs and bike lanes, low-emission standards for vehicles (including trucks and buses), industrial pollution reduction, and creating more green spaces. #sao-paulo #air-quality

Per WHO data cited in discussion, São Paulo saw a 45% reduction in PM2.5 concentration between 2010 and 2016; the city's "Rodizio" license-plate driving restriction, introduced in 2014, also cut car numbers, yet São Paulo still has among the worst air pollution in Latin America. #sao-paulo #air-quality

São Paulo enforces its low-emission policies through an environmental inspection program covering vehicle emissions and industrial pollution; violations can bring fines, license suspension, or criminal charges, while incentives include tax exemptions and subsidies for electric and hybrid vehicles. #sao-paulo #air-quality

São Paulo's persistent air pollution is attributed to heavy industry (transport, chemical, manufacturing), very high population density, valley geography surrounded by mountains that traps pollutants in stagnant weather, and public transport that is still overcrowded and unreliable. #sao-paulo #air-quality
